newsitem.title: Australia: Australian police charge Singaporean with murder.
newsitem.headline: Australian police charge Singaporean with murder.

text.p: Australian police said on Saturday they had charged a Singaporean student with the murder of two Indian students in the northern city of Brisbane.
The victims were Priya Ann D'Souza, 22, and her brother Ajay, 21, who had been living in Australia for about two years, police said by telephone from Brisbane.
Their bodies were found on Friday wrapped in plastic bags in bushland in Brisbane's western suburbs. An autopsy has been conducted, but police would not release the cause of death.
Their flatmate, 26-year-old engineering student Raajeshi Subramaniam, was charged with two counts of murder.
Subramaniam, who was arrested on Friday, also appeared in a Brisbane court earlier on Saturday on four counts of fraud.
Police would not give further details.
But the domestic news agency, Australian Associated Press, said the court was told Subramaniam had withdrawn almost A$10,000 (US$7,650) from the pair's bank account.
Subramaniam was refused bail and is being held in custody. He is due to appear in court again on Monday.
